questions.q: Who was on the bridge finding the ship's position at noon the next day?
choices: Captain Speedy
Phileas Fogg
The engineer
Passepartout

questions.q: Where was Captain Speedy while Fogg sailed the ship?
choices: Locked in his cabin, shouting angrily
Down below, working with the stokers
Asleep in a hammock on the main deck
Steering the ship from the stern rudder
questions.evidence: he was shut up in his cabin under lock and key

questions.q: How did Fogg get the crew to follow him instead of their captain?
choices: He showed them a letter from the ship's owners
He won them over with his banknotes
He promised each sailor a home in London
He frightened them with stories of pirates
questions.evidence: had so shrewdly managed with his banknotes

questions.q: What did Passepartout think of his master taking over the ship?
choices: He thought it was a crime and was ashamed
He thought it was simply glorious
He was afraid they would all be hanged
He wanted Fogg to free the captain at once
questions.evidence: he thought Mr. Fogg's manoeuvre simply glorious

questions.q: How did Passepartout get along with the sailors in the first days?
choices: He kept to himself and spoke to no one
He made warm friends and amazed them with acrobatics
He quarrelled with the stokers over how they fed the fires
He was seasick in his bunk most of the time
questions.evidence: He formed warm friendships with the sailors

questions.q: "His loquacious good-humour infected everyone." What does loquacious mean?
choices: Very quiet
Very talkative
Very tired
Very rude

questions.q: What did Fix begin to suspect about where the Henrietta was going?
choices: That it was heading back to New York
That Fogg was taking it somewhere safe, like a pirate
That the ship would sink before reaching land
That Fogg planned to hand him over to the angry crew at sea
questions.evidence: the robber, turned into a pirate, would quietly put himself in safety

questions.q: Why did the change in the wind on the 13th make the sails useless?
choices: It stopped blowing entirely
It blew from the south-east
It turned into a hurricane
It swung around to the north
questions.evidence: it remained obstinately in the south-east, rendering the sails useless

questions.q: What problem did the engineer report to Mr. Fogg on the 16th?
choices: There was a leak in the iron hull
There was not enough coal to go full steam to Liverpool
The crew was planning to free the captain from his cabin
The screw had been broken in the storm
questions.evidence: we haven't enough to go with all steam from New York to Liverpool

choices: Passepartout had dropped Fix's bag into the sea
Passepartout believed they really were going to Liverpool
Passepartout had laughed at Fix during the storm
Passepartout had told the whole crew that Fix was a detective
questions.evidence: Then you believe that we really are going to Liverpool?

questions.q: What order did Mr. Fogg give the engineer that evening?
choices: Let the fires go out to save the coal
Feed all the fires until the coal is exhausted
Turn the ship toward the nearest port for more coal
Raise the sails and stop the engine
questions.evidence: Feed all the fires until the coal is exhausted.

questions.q: Captain Speedy is called "a bomb" when he comes on deck. What does this tell you?
choices: He was carrying explosives
He was ready to burst with anger
He had been hurt in an accident
He was very small and round
questions.evidence: It was clear that he was on the point of bursting.

questions.q: Why did Mr. Fogg want to buy the Henrietta?
choices: To sell it later at a profit in Liverpool
To burn its upper part because the coal was gone
To give it as a gift to Passepartout
To keep the captain from reporting him to the police
questions.evidence: Yes; at least the upper part of her. The coal has given out.

questions.q: How much did Fogg pay for a ship the captain said was worth fifty thousand dollars?
choices: Twenty thousand dollars
Sixty thousand dollars
Forty thousand dollars
Eight thousand dollars

questions.q: How did Captain Speedy's feelings change once he had the money?
choices: He grew angrier and called Fogg a pirate again
He forgot his anger and paid Fogg a compliment
He demanded that Fogg give back his iron hull
He locked himself back in his cabin to sulk
questions.evidence: The captain forgot in an instant his anger

questions.q: Which parts of the ship were burned first, on the day Fogg bought her?
choices: The masts, rafts and spars
The poop, cabins, bunks and spare deck
The railings, the fittings and the top sides
The iron hull and the engine
questions.evidence: the poop, cabins, bunks, and the spare deck were sacrificed

questions.q: Why did Fogg decide to land at Queenstown instead of sailing on to Liverpool?
choices: The Henrietta was sinking and had to be left behind
Mail trains and fast boats from there would save him twelve hours
Captain Speedy refused to take the ship one mile further toward England
Fix wanted to arrest him in Ireland, not England
questions.evidence: Phileas Fogg counted on gaining twelve hours in the same way.

questions.q: What surprising thing happens at the very end of the chapter?
choices: Fogg misses the last train from Liverpool to London
Fix arrests Fogg on the Liverpool quay
Passepartout falls overboard near Dublin
Captain Speedy has Fogg arrested for piracy
questions.evidence: I arrest you in the Queen's name!
